title: Redwood discovery - model selection - OceanByte Labs
next_steps: Send tailored pricing + Dedicated vs Hosted cost examples
Schedule 1hr technical deep dive with infra team next week
Run 48hr benchmark on our 32k context model with customer prompts
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pricing sheet and feature matrix (due 2027-04-10)
Ravi Patel: Share benchmark template and request for sample prompt set (due 2027-04-09)
Ana Gomez: Schedule technical deep dive and invite infra folks (due 2027-04-12)
Hannah Cole (customer): Provide security questionnaire and SSO metadata (due 2027-04-11)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual document understanding and tool-calling. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private due to PII/data residency; main requirements: long context (20k-32k), multilingual support (EN/ES/FR/JA), robust tool-calling for retrieval and actions, and enterprise security controls. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security docs, and run a 48hr benchmark with sample prompts.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, we'll do quick intros and then dive into your model needs
00:10 James Rivera: hi im james, cto at oceanbyte, thanks for the time, we have priya and luca and hannah as well
00:18 Priya Natarajan: hey all, priya on ml eng, i'm leading model selection and inference roadmap
00:22 Luca Moretti: luca product -- curious about cost and latency tradeoffs
00:25 Hannah Cole: hannah security, i'll be focused on compliance and data flows
00:30 Maya Chen: awesome, quick agenda, context length, multilingual, tool-calling, hosting options, security Qs, then next steps
00:40 Ravi Patel: i'm ravi, i'll be technical lead on this call, we can get into latency/cost numbers and benchmarks
00:47 James Rivera: great, so high level -- why are we looking, we ingest long customer documents, contracts, support tickets, want a model that can do multi-doc summaries, question answering across 20k tokens, sometimes 30k, is that accurate priya?
01:05 Priya Natarajan: yes, we need 20k fairly often and occasional 32k windows for full contract context, also must support EN, ES, FR and japanese for some enterprise customers
01:18 Ana Gomez: noted, multilingual + long context -- that pushes towards 32k models or chunking with retrieval, do you prefer a single-pass long context or do you have an index/retrieval layer?
01:30 Priya Natarajan: we have an embedding store and vector search, but current experience loses cross-document context, so we want more native long-context to reduce hallucinations and keep tool-calls accurate
01:44 Ravi Patel: makes sense -- so two levers: use a long-context LLM (32k) or continue with 8k/16k model + more aggressive retrieval and tool orchestration. Each has latency and cost implications
01:58 Luca Moretti: can we get numbers, like per request cost delta or latency?
02:03 Ravi Patel: ballpark, hosted 32k open models are higher per-token cost but avoid extra round trips; on Dedicated you can reduce unit cost with batching and reserved capacity -- tradeoff is up-front commit
02:16 Maya Chen: also Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you data residency and control but more ops -- Hannah any constraints on that side?
02:26 Hannah Cole: we need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO/SAML. SOC 2 is table stakes, also looking at ISO 27001 and some customers need EU-only processing
02:39 Maya Chen: we support KMS/HSM and SSO, have audit logs, and for EU residency we can route to region or offer Private deployment
02:48 James Rivera: great, on models -- are you recommending specific open models? we've seen Llama 3 variants, Mistral, and some of the 70B open weights with 32k contexts
03:01 Ravi Patel: we often recommend testing a couple: Llama 3 70B 32k for instruction-following, Mistral Instruct if you want cost efficiency, and specialized long-context variants like mixtral-32k or qlora fine-tuned ones -- also Redwood provides verified performance profiles so you don't guess
03:18 Priya Natarajan: how about multilingual? Llama variants sometimes drop in japanese, any empirical data?
03:25 Ravi Patel: multicultural performance varies -- for JA/KO we see models trained with more multilingual data do better; Mistral-Instruct has decent EN/ES/FR but Japanese may need BLOOMZ or specialized models. We'll include cross-lingual evals in the benchmark.
03:41 Ana Gomez: also tool-calling: you mentioned tool-calling rules earlier -- we support structured function calling and streaming responses, and you can pin behavior via signature schemas, is that something you need?
03:54 Luca Moretti: yes, we need tool-calling for retrieval + a actions system to create tasks in our internal tracker, so the model needs to reliably produce structured responses and we should verify end-to-end
04:07 Ravi Patel: there's a difference between model native function calling support and runtime tool orchestration; some open models need an extra layer to parse and map to functions reliably -- Redwood's runtime can handle function signatures and fallback policies
04:21 Priya Natarajan: what about hallucination / grounding? we need deterministic cite-able extracts from source documents
04:28 Ana Gomez: recommended pattern is RAG with citation prompts, model scoring for confidence, and Redwood can attach source highlights via our retrieval + tool pipeline. Also prefix/KV caching helps with repeated sections in contracts
04:41 James Rivera: latency concerns -- if we do long-context 32k, what's latency look like for a typical 2k-token output?
04:49 Ravi Patel: depends on hardware; hosted with optimized runtime we see 2k token generation in ~700ms-2s on high-end GPUs for many models; Dedicated reduces variability and improves p50/p95. But quantized/open weights can be slower or faster depending on kernel support
05:07 Hannah Cole: on security -- can you detail encryption at rest and in transit and key management options?
05:13 Maya Chen: yes, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM for Private deployments; we can provide SOC2 docs and SSO metadata
05:29 Priya Natarajan: we also need to understand data retention policies for embeddings and logs
05:35 Maya Chen: configurable retention windows, and Dedicated/Private can keep data isolated; hosted defaults to 30 days for debug logs but embeddings retention can be controlled -- we'll put exact values in the security pack
05:48 Luca Moretti: competitors -- any specific reasons customers pick Redwood vs Anthropic or OpenAI?
05:53 Maya Chen: mainly production controls, model catalog transparency, dedicated capacity options and cost levers; we surface quantization and batching recommendations via Redwood Optimize which helps lower unit costs
06:07 Priya Natarajan: about evaluation -- we'd like to run our own benchmarks with our prompt set and multi-lang docs, you mentioned a 48hr sandbox?
06:16 Ravi Patel: yes, propose a 48hr benchmark where we host a Dedicated trial or run in Hosted with agreed throughput; we'll execute tests across Llama 3 70B 32k, mixtral-32k and a more efficient Mistral variant, compare latency, cost, and multilingual F1/ROUGE-like metrics
06:34 James Rivera: is there a way to simulate peak load? we expect bursts around contract close times
06:39 Ana Gomez: yes, Dedicated has autoscaling policies and burst capacity; we can mimic your traffic shape during the benchmark
06:47 Hannah Cole: legal & procurement -- what's required for a Private deployment procurement timeline?
06:52 Maya Chen: Private can take longer -- contract + security review + deployment provisioning typically 6-10 weeks depending on infra, Dedicated is quicker with reserved capacity options
07:04 Luca Moretti: funding -- cost model questions again, do you have examples for a 100 reqs/min workload?
07:09 Ravi Patel: we'll run cost modeling in the pricing sheet; generally Dedicated gives lowest per-token when committed, Hosted is pay-as-you-go but higher unit cost
07:20 Priya Natarajan: do you support model pinning and rollbacks?
07:23 Maya Chen: yes, pin a version, can canary and rollback; we also provide per-route latency and cost dashboards
07:32 James Rivera: ok can we recap action items?
07:35 Maya Chen: sure -- we'll send pricing and feature matrix, security pack, schedule deep dive, and start the benchmark once we get sample prompts
07:44 Priya Natarajan: i'll share sample prompt set and a small doc corpus, along with security questionnaire
07:50 Maya Chen: perfect, thanks everyone
07:52 Ravi Patel: thanks, talk soon
07:55 Meeting end
